# A Go package using logos/enum behaves identically under the plain
# toolchain and the logos toolchain, and eject vendors it into the
# support module so the ejected tree builds under plain go. The
# vendored path follows the generic supportRelPath rule (logos/enum
# maps to enum under the rt support root); the dense index values
# below are the enum guarantee, not the wiring.
env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

cd m

go run .
stdout '^0 1 2 3 1 -1$'
cp stdout $WORK/gorun.txt

logos run .
cmp stdout $WORK/gorun.txt

# Eject keeps the enum table working through the vendored support module.
logos eject -o out
exists out/main.go
exists out/_logos_deps/rt/enum/enum.go
grep 'gosuda/loGos/rt/enum' out/main.go

cd out
go run .
cmp stdout $WORK/gorun.txt

-- m/go.mod --
module example.com/enumtable

go 1.27

-- m/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"logos/enum"
)

type color int

const (
	red color = iota
	green
	blue
)

var colors = []color{red, green, blue}

type sparse int

const (
	sA sparse = 4
	sB sparse = 6
	sC sparse = 2
)

var sparsers = []sparse{sA, sB, sC}

func main() {
	fmt.Println(
		enum.Index(colors, red),
		enum.Index(colors, green),
		enum.Index(colors, blue),
		enum.Count(colors),
		enum.Index(sparsers, sB),
		enum.Index(sparsers, sparse(3)),
	)
}
